en.question: Which statement about tokens is accurate for budgeting purposes?

options.text: One token corresponds to one word, so word count is a reliable proxy.
options.note: Long or unusual words split into several tokens; common short words may be one.

options.text: Only generated output is tokenised and billed; supplied input is not.
options.note: Input is billed too, and in most applications it dominates the bill.

options.text: Whitespace and punctuation are excluded from the token count.
options.note: Whitespace and punctuation consume tokens like any other characters.

options.text: Tokens are sub-word units, roughly three to four characters of English.

en.explanation: Tokens are sub-word fragments. The three-to-four-character heuristic is fine for rough English planning but understates code, nested JSON, and non-Latin scripts, so use token counting when the number matters.
